Internet Microdoses
A three-hour concert film is selling out cinemas. It made more on its opening weekend than any music documentary in twenty years. Bring snacks. Get tickets →
A library the size of a phone box opened on a high street. It holds 200 books and lends them on trust. So far, nothing has gone missing. Visit it →
A boat that sank 4,000 years ago turned up in a field. Archaeologists found it while checking ground for a new road. Dig in →
A football club named its new font after a former captain. It’s on the shirts, the tickets and the stadium signs. See the font →
Students are holding drawing classes in train stations. Bring a pencil; stools are provided. Find a class →

Aesthetic Study · Turning the page

Last year it was fashionable to be seen reading on the train. This year, the book itself is the accessory: tote bags with bookshelves printed on them, cafés with reading-only tables, book-club dinners that sell out in minutes.

Whatever the reason, more people are carrying books. Some are even reading them.
Judge a book by its cover
A moment with
Ines Calder
Founder of Calder & Co.

values.altText: Portrait of a woman by a lake

values.text:
Ines Calder makes furniture from salvaged wood and wants every piece to look like it has a past. Her third collection launches this month.

Where do your ideas come from?
Old buildings, mostly. I keep a photo of every door I like.

Three places that inspire you?
1. A timber yard by the river
2. A library reading room
3. My grandmother’s kitchen

Write us a fortune cookie.
The thing you keep fixing is the thing you love.
Read the full interview

Object Love · The bent chair

A chair bent from a single sheet of plywood, first made in the 1940s and still in production. It weighs about as much as a cat. Look closely and there isn’t a screw in it.

Quick Hits

Put a photo on your keychain with a tiny camera.
A museum is lit only by candles for one night.
Discover a dictionary of words you can’t read.

Reader Question

Last week we asked: if you opened a tiny museum, what would be in it? Our favourite answer: “Every key I’ve ever kept without knowing what it opens.”

This week: what’s the most useful thing you own that cost less than $5? Reply and tell us.

All booked up,
Tom
